items.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007
items.q: And I do listen to people like Charles Brown or you know, I listen to all kinds of people. But when I heard him live, that really got in.

ctx.x: Do you spend a lot of time listening? I mean when you’re at home and you’ve got a day off, are you a person who deliberately goes and puts on music as you do your —

Never as I’m doing anything. I can’t listen to music when I drive, it’s really dangerous. I’ve tried. And I can’t do both things. I’m not good — I don’t like background music at © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

all. But sometimes I will — I don’t listen to music like I used to before I became so involved in it. I mean I really just don’t. But I do, like at festivals I get to hear other people and sometimes I’ll go out and hear other people. My life right now, I have people at home I take care of. My mother-in-law lives with me and my mother is close by. And so I don’t go out as much as I did or will in the future sometime. I mean I certainly plan to spend more time listening to other people. But I love hearing live…
